wives.title: Wives of the Prophet ﷺ
wives.intro: The eleven Ummahatul Mu'minin (Mothers of the Believers) who shared the household of the Prophet. Each marriage carried profound humanitarian, educational, social, or diplomatic wisdom.

b: Married when the Prophet was twenty-five and Khadijah was forty. Throughout her lifetime with him, the Prophet took no other wife.
The first person to embrace Islam, his pillar of support during the first revelation, and the mother in whose home the family grew. All the Prophet's children were born to her, except Ibrahim.
Passed away in the tenth year of prophethood — the same year as Abu Talib's passing.
Married about a month after Khadijah's passing — his first marriage after that period of grief.
Previously married to Sakran bin Amr, her cousin, who passed away after they migrated to Abyssinia.
Passed away in Madinah in Shawwal, 54 AH.
The only wife of the Prophet who had not been previously married, and the most beloved to him.
The most knowledgeable in jurisprudence among women and exceptionally intelligent — her narrations form a primary source of knowledge regarding the Prophet's household life.
It was in her room that the Prophet was nursed during his final illness, passed away, and was buried. She passed away on 17 Ramadan 57 or 58 AH and was buried in Baqi'.
Widowed after her husband, Khunais bin Hudhafah as-Sahmi, passed away between the battles of Badr and Uhud.
Married by the Prophet after her waiting period. The first compiled manuscript of the Quran during Abu Bakr's caliphate was later entrusted to her care.
Passed away in Madinah in Sha'ban 45 AH at age sixty, buried in Baqi'.
From Bani Hilal bin Amir. Titled Ummul Masakin — Mother of the Poor — due to her immense compassion and generosity toward them.
Previously married to Abdullah bin Jahsh, who fell at Uhud.
Shared only two or three months with the Prophet before passing away in Rabi'ul Akhir 4 AH. The Prophet personally led her funeral prayer and buried her in Baqi'.
Wife of Abu Salamah, the noble companion who passed away in Jumad al-Akhir 4 AH leaving several children.
An exceptionally wise jurist. Her advice during Hudaibiyah — encouraging the Prophet to shave and sacrifice first — resolved the deadlock of the entire company.
Passed away in 59 or 62 AH at age eighty-four, buried in Baqi'.
Daughter of the Prophet's paternal aunt, from Bani Asad bin Khuzaimah. Previously married to Zaid bin Harithah, who was formerly considered an adopted son of the Prophet.
This marriage abolished pre-Islamic customs equating adopted sons with biological sons — a decree explained directly in Surah al-Ahzab.
Devoted to worship and charity. She passed away in 20 AH at age fifty-three — the first wife to join the Prophet after his passing; Umar bin Khattab led her funeral prayer.
Daughter of the chief of Bani Mustaliq. Initially captured by Thabit bin Qais, she contracted a ransom agreement for her freedom.
The Prophet paid her ransom and married her. Consequently, Muslims freed one hundred captives of Bani Mustaliq as new relatives of the Messenger — a marriage resulting in mass liberation.
Passed away in Rabi'ul Awwal 56 AH at age around sixty-five.
Daughter of Abu Sufyan. Migrated to Abyssinia with her husband, Abdullah bin Jahsh, who apostatized and died there — leaving her alone in a foreign land holding firmly to her faith.
The Prophet dispatched Amr bin Umayyah to the Negus with a proposal. The Negus performed the marriage and provided a dowry of four hundred dinars.
Their household life began after the Prophet returned from Khaibar. She passed away around 42–50 AH.
Daughter of Huyay bin Akhtab, chief of Jewish Bani Nadhir. Taken as captive at Khaibar before the Prophet chose her for himself.
When invited to Islam, she willingly accepted. The Prophet granted her freedom, making her freedom her dowry.
The marriage commenced at Saddi Shahba', twelve miles from Khaibar. She passed away around 50 AH and was buried in Baqi'.
Sister of Ummul Fadhl Lubabah bint Harith, extending kinship ties with tribes around Makkah.
According to authentic accounts, the Prophet married her during Dzulqa'dah during Umrah Qadha'.
The last wife he married.

kids.title: Children of the Prophet ﷺ
kids.intro: His seven children — three sons and four daughters. All were born to Lady Khadijah bint Khuwailid, except Ibrahim who was born to Mariyah al-Qibthiyah. All three sons passed away in childhood.

b: The firstborn son, from whom the Prophet's honorific honor Abul Qasim was taken. Passed away in early childhood.
Married Abul Ash bin Rabi'. The narrative of her migration to Madinah and her husband's eventual conversion is one of the most touching in the Sirah.
Married Uthman bin Affan and migrated with him to Abyssinia and then Madinah. Passed away during the Battle of Badr, which was why Uthman was excused to nurse her while earning Badr rewards.
Married Uthman bin Affan after Ruqayyah's passing — earning Uthman the honorific Dzun Nurain (Possessor of Two Lights) for marrying two daughters of the Prophet sequentially.
Married Ali bin Abu Talib between Badr and Uhud. From this marriage were born Hasan, Husain, Zainab, and Ummu Kultsum.
The only child surviving at the Prophet's passing; she joined her father about six months later.
Titles at-Tayyib and at-Tahir. Passed away in childhood like his brothers.
The only child born to Mariyah al-Qibthiyah, born in Madinah in 8 AH.
Passed away at around eighteen months old. When a solar eclipse coincided with his passing, the Prophet affirmed that eclipses are signs of Allah, not caused by anyone's death or birth.
